# agent-browser core

Fast browser automation CLI for AI agents. Chrome/Chromium via CDP, no
Playwright or Puppeteer dependency. Accessibility-tree snapshots with compact
`@eN` refs let agents interact with pages in ~200-400 tokens instead of
parsing raw HTML.

Most normal web tasks (navigate, read, click, fill, extract, screenshot) are
covered here. Load a specialized skill when the task falls outside browser
web pages — see [When to load another skill](#when-to-load-another-skill).

## The core loop

```bash
agent-browser open <url>        # 1. Open a page
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 2. See what's on it (interactive elements only)
agent-browser click @e3         # 3. Act on refs from the snapshot
agent-browser snapshot -i       # 4. Re-snapshot after any page change
```

Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, ...) are assigned fresh on every snapshot. They become
**stale the moment the page changes** — after clicks that navigate, form
submits, dynamic re-renders, dialog opens. Always re-snapshot before your
next ref interaction.

## Quickstart

```bash
# Install once
npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install

# Take a screenshot of a page
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser screenshot home.png
agent-browser close

# Search, click a result, and capture it
agent-browser open https://duckduckgo.com
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # find the search box ref
agent-browser fill @e1 "agent-browser cli"
agent-browser press Enter
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i                      # refs now reflect results
agent-browser click @e5                        # click a result
agent-browser screenshot result.png
```

The browser stays running across commands so these feel like a single
session. Use `agent-browser close` (or `close --all`) when you're done.

## Reading a page

```bash
agent-browser snapshot                    # full tree (verbose)
agent-browser snapshot -i                 # interactive elements only (preferred)
agent-browser snapshot -i -u              # include href urls on links
agent-browser snapshot -i -c              # compact (no empty structural nodes)
agent-browser snapshot -i -d 3            # cap depth at 3 levels
agent-browser snapshot -s "#main"         # scope to a CSS selector
agent-browser snapshot -i --json          # machine-readable output
```

Snapshot output looks like:

```
Page: Example - Log in
URL: https://example.com/login

@e1 [heading] "Log in"
@e2 [form]
  @e3 [input type="email"] placeholder="Email"
  @e4 [input type="password"] placeholder="Password"
  @e5 [button type="submit"] "Continue"
  @e6 [link] "Forgot password?"
```

For unstructured reading (no refs needed):

```bash
agent-browser get text @e1                # visible text of an element
agent-browser get html @e1                # innerHTML
agent-browser get attr @e1 href           # any attribute
agent-browser get value @e1               # input value
agent-browser get title                   # page title
agent-browser get url                     # current URL
agent-browser get count ".item"           # count matching elements
```

## Interacting

```bash
agent-browser click @e1                   # click
agent-browser click @e1 --new-tab         # open link in new tab instead of navigating
agent-browser dblclick @e1                # double-click
agent-browser hover @e1                   # hover
agent-browser focus @e1                   # focus (useful before keyboard input)
agent-browser fill @e2 "hello"            # clear then type
agent-browser type @e2 " world"           # type without clearing
agent-browser press Enter                 # press a key at current focus
agent-browser press Control+a             # key combination
agent-browser check @e3                   # check checkbox
agent-browser uncheck @e3                 # uncheck
agent-browser select @e4 "option-value"   # select dropdown option
agent-browser select @e4 "a" "b"          # select multiple
agent-browser upload @e5 file1.pdf        # upload file(s)
agent-browser scroll down 500             # scroll page (up/down/left/right)
agent-browser scrollintoview @e1          # scroll element into view
agent-browser drag @e1 @e2                # drag and drop
```

### When refs don't work or you don't want to snapshot

Use semantic locators:

```bash
agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
agent-browser find text "Sign In" click --exact     # exact match only
agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
agent-browser find placeholder "Search" type "query"
agent-browser find testid "submit-btn" click
agent-browser find first ".card" click
agent-browser find nth 2 ".card" hover
```

Or a raw CSS selector:

```bash
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser fill "input[name=email]" "user@test.com"
agent-browser click "button.primary"
```

Rule of thumb: snapshot + `@eN` refs are fastest and most reliable for
AI agents. `find role/text/label` is next best and doesn't require a prior
snapshot. Raw CSS is a fallback when the others fail.

## Waiting (read this)

Agents fail more often from bad waits than from bad selectors. Pick the
right wait for the situation:

```bash
agent-browser wait @e1                     # until an element appears

# Slice 1: editor shell (#1)

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|

input.message:
Slice 1 (#1, editor shell) is implemented on `feat/editor-shell` in 6 local commits (not pushed, no PR, no ADR conflicts). Acceptance criteria were checked in a real browser with agent-browser.

## Commits (no trailers)
```
2a55e48 chore: scaffold vite react ts tooling
e1852c4 feat: openrouter dev proxy and key flag
93ee1eb feat: document storage, autosave and sample
0a6e45d feat: styled markdown editor
549c967 feat: app shell, hint and missing-key banner
dada03c docs: slice 1 verification
```

## Files and src layout
Worktree root: `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `tsconfig.json`, `biome.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `.env.example`.

```
config/openrouter-proxy.ts (+ .test.ts)
src/main.tsx, index.css (@theme static tokens), env.d.ts (declares __HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__)
src/editor/   theme.ts, extensions.ts, create-editor-view.ts, code-block-lines.ts (+ .test.ts)
src/ui/       App.tsx, EditorPane.tsx, Hint.tsx, MissingKeyBanner.tsx, platform.ts (+ .test.ts)
src/document/ sample-document.ts, storage.ts, autosave.ts (+ tests for each)
docs/chiri/verification/1-editor-shell.md, img/1-{1,2,3}.png
```
Deviations from AGENTS.md's layout, to note in the PR:
- New `src/document/` folder for the sample Document, storage and autosave.
- New top-level `config/` folder for the pure proxy builder and its test, so it is unit-testable and not buried in `vite.config.ts`.
- `docs/chiri/verification/1-editor-shell.md` plus 3 screenshots, which you did not explicitly ask for. They record the browser check. The doc says no AI calls were made. I did not touch `ai-costs.md`.

## Dependencies (installed)
- **Runtime:**
  - react 19.3.1, react-dom 19.3.1
  - @codemirror/state 6.7.6, view 6.43.15, commands 6.11.1, language 6.13.1, lang-markdown 6.5.2
  - @lezer/highlight 1.2.5
  - @fontsource-variable/inter 5.3.0, @fontsource-variable/league-spartan 5.3.0
- **Dev:**
  - vite 8.3.5, vitest 5.0.5, typescript 7.0.2 (the native compiler; `tsc` works)
  - @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.2, tailwindcss 4.3.3, @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3
  - @biomejs/biome 2.6.3
  - @types/react 19.3.0, @types/react-dom 19.3.0
  - @types/node 22.20.5, pinned to `^22` on purpose to match the Node 22 engine instead of the newer 26 types

`engines.node` is `>=22.12.0` (Vite 8 and Vitest 5 require 22.12 or later), and `packageManager` is `pnpm@11.17.0`.

## Results
- **`pnpm test`:** 6 files, 30 tests, all green. Red-first runs were done for every pure module.
  - Storage load/save: fake Storage, a throwing Storage and a null Storage.
  - Autosave: debounce, flush and cancel with fake timers.
  - Proxy builder: path rewrite, and Authorization overwritten on every request, including a browser-sent one.
  - `codeBlockLineStarts`, which gives fenced and indented code lines a background.
  - Sample Document: word count and structure.
  - `platform.ts`: Mac versus Ctrl+K label.
- **`pnpm biome check`:** 27 files, zero diagnostics. `css.parser.tailwindDirectives` is on, and `*.md`, `.claude` and `docs` are excluded. The first `--write` run reformatted AGENTS.md, GLOSSARY.md and the PR template (Biome 2.6 formats Markdown); I reverted that and excluded `*.md`.
- **`pnpm build`:** `tsc --noEmit` plus `vite build`, green, with a 731 kB JS bundle. I set `chunkSizeWarningLimit` to 900 to keep the output quiet.
- **Secrets:** `grep -r "sk-or-" dist/` finds nothing, and the key value is not in `dist` either. The string `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` appears once in the bundle, as banner text only.
- **Servers:** `pnpm dev` and `pnpm preview` both serve HTML (200). I stopped all servers and no `.env` was created.

## Browser check (agent-browser)
- **First visit:** the sample Document and the hint show. Headings are larger and bolder, with dimmed marks. Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links and fenced code render as intended.
- **Fonts:** League Spartan is on the `h1` only; Inter is on the body and the editor.
- **Persistence:** after typing and a reload, the text is restored. `Object.keys(localStorage)` is only `["chiri.document"]`.
- **Proxy with a key:** the browser sent `Bearer placeholder` and `/api/openrouter/models` returned 200 (464 models).
- **Proxy without a key:** the banner shows, `__HAS_OPENROUTER_KEY__` is false, and a proxied call returns 401.
- **Other:** no horizontal scroll at 375 px, and the same proxy works under `vite preview`.
- **Screenshot trick:** CodeMirror virtualizes lines, so a short viewport renders only part of the Document. I used a 1280x1500 viewport for the full-document screenshot.

## Things to know
1. **A real `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is already in this shell's environment.** `loadEnv(mode, cwd, '')` includes `process.env`, so the proxy picked it up even with no `.env`. That is why `/auth/key` and `/models` worked here. I tested the missing-key banner by starting a second dev server with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=` set empty. The agent-browser `eval` that fetched `/auth/key` printed a masked key label into my tool output, but I never printed the key value. The key did not leak into the bundle or the repo.
2. **Empty key:** the proxy always sets `Authorization: Bearer ${key}`, so with an empty key it sends `Bearer ` and OpenRouter answers 401. That matches your spec, and the placeholder is still never forwarded.
3. **No-key first visit:** nothing is written to `localStorage` until the first edit, so the stored key is the Document string only.
4. **Config import:** `vite.config.ts` imports `./config/openrouter-proxy.ts` with the extension. Without it, Vite 8 warns about its native config loader. That needs `allowImportingTsExtensions` in `tsconfig.json`.
5. **List continuation:** the Markdown keymap (list and quote continuation on Enter) comes from `@codemirror/lang-markdown`'s default `addKeymap`. Pressing Enter on an empty `>` quote line does not exit the quote in my manual test. I left the library default alone.
6. **Hint:** it reads "Select text and press ⌘K" on Apple platforms and "Select text and press Ctrl+K" elsewhere; it rendered as Ctrl+K here, and only the formatter logic is unit-tested.

## Sample Document
It is 331 words (whitespace split of the whole Markdown) and reads as an internal "Release process update: weekday deploys" announcement. It has a `#` title, two `##` sections, a bullet list and a fenced bash block. Planted flaws:
1. **Overlong sentence:** the first paragraph, one run-on sentence starting "For the past two years our team has frozen all production deployments on Fridays, a rule introduced after…".
2. **Tone shift:** "Honestly, the old freeze was a total pain and everyone kinda hated it. So we're ditching it, no big deal… lol."
3. **Typo:** "you will recieve a prompt".
4. **Redundant passage:** "All deploys need a reviewed pull request. Nothing may be deployed without a review. Every deployment has to be approved by a reviewer first."
5. **List:** non-parallel items with inconsistent punctuation: "Tests are passing on the main branch", "Get a review from a second engineer", "Rollback plan, you must write one in the pull request.", "No deploys during the on-call handover".
